process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Apply online
process.description: Apply through www.tnmedicalselection.net. The portal is open from 12:00 noon on 9th October 2026 until 5:00 PM on 15th October 2026, by server time. Submit one complete application; particulars cannot be changed after submission. No extension is provided. Fill the form yourself and check the site for updates. The prospectus itself is available online free of cost.

process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Submitting the application accepts the counselling scheme
process.description: By completing the online application/registration form, candidates are deemed to have read, agreed to and accepted the NEET-PG 2026 counselling scheme and its terms and conditions. Clause 40 separately states that applicants are deemed to have agreed to the prospectus and “will not have the right to challenge” any clause.

process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Upload the required documents
process.description: Upload all relevant, visibly clear, self-attested copies with the application. Service candidates must upload their service particulars certified by the forwarding authority with date and seal before the deadline. An incomplete application or unclear/missing mandatory documents will be summarily rejected. The required document list is also reproduced in Annexure I. The prospectus says a rejected application will not be reconsidered and no correspondence/request for reconsideration will be entertained.

process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Pay the application and round fees
process.description: The online application fee is ₹3,000 and is non-refundable, except that Tamil Nadu native Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Caste (Arunthathiyar) and Scheduled Tribe candidates are exempt. Counselling registration fees are separate: ₹1,000 for Round 1, ₹1,000 for Round 3 in the stated cases, and ₹1,000 for the Stray Vacancy Round in the stated cases. Confirm whether any Round 2 fee applies; the prospectus does not say.

process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Rank list and seat allotment
process.description: The State Rank List is based on NEET-PG 2026 marks and, for eligible in-service candidates who qualified NEET-PG, the additional service weightage described in the prospectus. Online allotment is by rank with the Tamil Nadu reservation roster. The provisional rank list will be published after application scrutiny; its date is to be notified.

process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Participate in online counselling
process.description: The prospectus provides Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 and a Stray Vacancy Round. Dates and joining windows will be announced later. Changes notified by DGHS/MCC or court orders will apply when notified to State counselling.

process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Report to the allotted institution
process.description: The allotment/admission process is online under the stated online-only rule. Separately, download the provisional allotment order and join at the allotted Medical College within its stated date/time, producing the specified originals and scanned copies. Pay the applicable tuition/special fees through the stated process. The source does not describe physical reporting as an entirely online step.

process.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Follow official notices
process.description: Check www.tnmedicalselection.net frequently throughout counselling for schedules, changes, results and notices. The Selection Committee says it will not contact candidates individually and is not responsible for missed website notices.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Use the online Selection Committee portal
process.description: Apply through www.tnmedicalselection.net. The Selection Committee says notices, updates, results and other admissions information will be published there; candidates should check it frequently because individual contact will not be made.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Apply online and submit documents
process.description: The application and supporting documents must be submitted online. Offline admissions and resignations are not permitted. Upload visibly clear, self-attested copies; incomplete applications or applications with unclear documents will not be accepted.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Submit one accurate application yourself
process.description: Candidates are advised to submit only one online application, complete every mandatory field, and enter true and correct information. The application is to be filled by the candidate, not an agent, third party or consultancy. Submitted particulars cannot be changed; incomplete applications are not accepted. The prospectus says that if an application is rejected, no correspondence or request for reconsideration will be entertained.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Pay online
process.description: The application fee is paid through the online payment portal using debit card, credit card, net banking, RTGS or UPI. A bank account deduction alone is not proof that payment succeeded. No extension of the application deadline is provided.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Provisional state rank list
process.description: After scrutiny of applications, the Selection Committee publishes a provisional state rank list on www.tnmedicalselection.net. The state rank list is based on NEET PG 2026 marks.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Register for counselling rounds
process.description: Counselling registration costs ₹1,000 and is non-refundable. Round 3 and Stray Vacancy Round each separately mention a ₹1,000 registration fee for specified candidates; see the round rules for who pays.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Download the allotment order and join
process.description: Download the provisional allotment order and join the allotted college on or before the date and time stated in that order. The full tuition and special fees must be paid online when downloading the order.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Keep admission and resignation online
process.description: All admissions and resignations must be completed online. The prospectus says offline admission or resignation will not be accepted and warns that colleges conducting it may face legal consequences.

process.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB service-candidate applications use the Selection Committee website
process.description: Apply through www.tnmedicalselection.net. The prospectus, application, updates, rank list, notices and counselling information are published there. The Selection Committee says it will not contact candidates individually; follow the site throughout the process.

process.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB application documents must be uploaded online
process.description: Upload all necessary documents with the online application. Only clear, self-attested copies should be uploaded. Offline documents are not accepted; incomplete applications or applications with unclear documents will be summarily rejected.

process.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Submit one complete DNB application
process.description: Submit only one online application and complete every mandatory field. After final submission, changes to particulars will not be accepted under any circumstances. No extension of the application time will be entertained. Ensure that all information entered in the online application is true and correct.

process.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB application payments are online only
process.description: Use the online payment portal by debit card, credit card, net banking, RTGS or UPI. A bank-account deduction alone is not proof that payment succeeded; check transaction limits and check payment status of payment.

process.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Submitting the DNB application accepts the counselling terms
process.description: On completing online submission/registration, candidates are treated as having read, agreed to and accepted the 2026-2027 DNB counselling scheme and prospectus terms. The Selection Committee says rejected applications will not be reconsidered by correspondence.

process.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Counselling-scheme acceptance on submission
process.description: Completing the online application/registration deems the candidate to have read, agreed to and accepted the NEET-PG 2026 counselling scheme and all its terms and conditions.

listedHomeInstitutions.label: Check the medical qualification and nativity routes below

inServiceLabel.label: Meet the Tamil Nadu service-candidate definition for the programme you seek, including its appointment route, continuous service, certification and remaining-service requirements. Check the MD/MS/Diploma and DNB definitions separately.
inServiceLabel.note: The prospectus does not identify an online in-service list. The profile answer must be checked against the exact categories and service records in the prospectus.

rules.title: These prospectuses cover medical courses
rules.explanation: The supplied Tamil Nadu prospectuses cover MD/MS, medical Diploma and the specified DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma courses. They do not cover MDS counselling.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Qualify NEET-PG 2026
rules.explanation: You must qualify NEET-PG 2026 and meet the qualifying criteria applied by the Director General of Health Services and the current postgraduate medical education rules. The prospectus says to check the NBE Information Bulletin for the detailed qualifying criteria.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: NEET-PG qualifying percentile and score
rules.explanation: The table prints these minimums out of 800: General, 50th percentile / 262; SC/ST/OBC including person with disability, 40th percentile / 226; General Persons with Disability, 45th percentile / 244. The prose says General candidates in Tamil Nadu need the 50th percentile; Tamil Nadu natives in SC, SCA, ST, BC, BCM, MBC or DNC need the 40th percentile; and SC-PH/ST-PH/OBC-PH need the 40th percentile. Check which minimum applies to your exact Tamil Nadu nativity, community and disability status.
rules.note: The brochure's table and prose state overlapping category scopes, and the profile does not record NEET percentile/score or the Tamil Nadu subcategories. No automatic threshold decision is made.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Nationality and OCI status
rules.explanation: The prospectus first says candidates should be citizens of India. It then says Indian nationals, OCI cardholders, Persons of Indian Origin and foreign nationals may be eligible subject to government/institution rules, and says OCI cardholders are treated on par with Indian citizens and eligible for Open (General) category seats. Confirm your status with the Selection Committee before relying on this clause.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Tamil Nadu native and community route
rules.explanation: Candidates claiming Tamil Nadu nativity who completed MBBS, including CRMI/CRRI internship, either in Tamil Nadu or outside the State may apply under their corresponding community for Government Medical College seats and Government Quota seats in Self-Financing Medical Institutions. The prospectus requires a competent Tamil Nadu Revenue Department nativity certificate. It does not define every route for establishing nativity, so have the Committee confirm your certificate and route.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Other-State native with MBBS in Tamil Nadu
rules.explanation: A candidate native to another State who completed MBBS, including CRMI/CRRI internship, in Tamil Nadu is eligible only under Open category for the Government Medical College and Government Quota seats described here. The profile has no Tamil Nadu nativity fact or Open-category allotment control, so confirm this manually. This stated other-State-native route requires MBBS including internship in Tamil Nadu. Clause 10(ii) says candidates outside the clause 5 routes are not eligible; the prospectus does not establish Government Quota eligibility for an other-State native with MBBS outside Tamil Nadu. Check the exact nativity/qualification route manually rather than substituting domicile.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Nativity and dual nativity
rules.explanation: A Tamil Nadu nativity claim requires a certificate issued by the competent Tamil Nadu Revenue Department authority with official seal. The prospectus says action will be taken against candidates claiming dual nativity. Candidates claiming Tamil Nadu nativity and community reservation must also upload the community certificates described in the document list.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Tamil Nadu community reservation documents
rules.explanation: Tamil Nadu candidates claiming BC, BC (Muslim), MBC, Denotified Community, SC, SCA or ST status must provide the required Tamil Nadu community certificate. The prospectus also requires a community certificate for either parent when claiming both Tamil Nadu nativity and community reservation. See the community lists in the annexure and confirm the exact listed community and certificate authority.
rules.note: The profile category options do not distinguish BC, BCM, MBC/DNC or SCA and cannot safely determine Tamil Nadu community reservation.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Complete CRRI/CRMI by the deadline
rules.explanation: You must have passed MBBS and completed or be completing CRRI/CRMI on or before 30th September 2026. The prospectus requires documentary proof of registration with the National Medical Commission, erstwhile Medical Council of India or a State Medical Council at counselling/admission.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Recognized MBBS degree and University eligibility certificate
rules.explanation: You must hold an MBBS degree awarded by Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University or another University recognized by the Medical Council of India. If you qualified from another University, produce an eligibility certificate from Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University, Guindy, Chennai, at admission.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Current-year diploma candidates applying for a degree
rules.explanation: A candidate pursuing a Diploma course, including an All India Quota Diploma, may apply for a postgraduate degree course in the same academic year if the Diploma is completed before the counselling process begins; the prospectus identifies the online-application notification date as the start of that process.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Currently pursuing a postgraduate course
rules.explanation: Candidates currently undergoing a postgraduate degree, DNB, equivalent or Diploma course are not eligible to apply for a postgraduate degree or Diploma course under this prospectus.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Previously completed postgraduate qualification
rules.explanation: Candidates who have completed a postgraduate degree, DNB or equivalent are not eligible for another postgraduate degree or Diploma course. A candidate who already holds a Diploma cannot apply for another Diploma, but may apply for a postgraduate degree.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Who qualifies as an in-service candidate
rules.explanation: For allotment as a service candidate, the prospectus includes (1) medical officers selected by TNPSC/MRB through a competitive written examination or special qualifying examination and appointed in Tamil Nadu Medical Services, with at least two years of continuous service as of 31st March 2026; and (2) medical officers serving in Tamil Nadu local bodies, with at least two years of continuous service as of 31st March 2026. Upload the certified service proforma and supporting service particulars. Officers working in institutions under the Registered Societies Act or in Self-Financing Institutions are considered non-service candidates. A Medical Officer working in a Government institution/local body who applies as a private candidate while concealing service status faces summary rejection and cancellation of any allotment.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Service candidates outside the stated service criteria
rules.explanation: Clause 12(b), under the heading “Non-eligibility for Service Quota”, says temporarily appointed candidates who have not completed two years of continuous service as on 31st March 2026 under clause 12(a)(i) are “not eligible to apply for Post Graduate admission in 2026-2027 session”. Their application will be summarily rejected even if inadvertently certified by a competent authority. The heading and broad admission wording should be confirmed for the candidate route; this Government-quota clause is not imposed on Management/NRI applicants.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Minimum service remaining after the course
rules.explanation: The service-candidate instructions say applicants under the service quota must have at least five years of service left at the end of their postgraduate degree or Diploma course. Read this with the separate post-course service undertakings and confirm how the Committee applies it to your retirement date. Exactly five years is not assigned to either the “more than five” or “less than five” bond group, although the eligibility clause says at least five years. Confirm this boundary with the Selection Committee.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Additional service weightage
rules.explanation: Eligible service candidates who qualified NEET-PG shall be awarded additional weightage of up to 10% of their NEET-PG eligible marks for each year of service completed in hilly/remote and/or difficult or rural areas, subject to a maximum of 30% of marks secured in NEET-PG 2026. The prospectus cites G.O. (Ms.) Nos.86, 114 and 423 and gives no current station list or calculation details.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Persons with benchmark disabilities
rules.explanation: The prospectus reserves 5% of total seats available in Government Medical Institutions for persons with benchmark disabilities. It says disability of 40–80% may be considered eligible; less than 40% is eligible to apply under General category but not for the PwD reservation; and more than 80% is not eligible for admission. The accompanying disability matrix gives additional disability-specific criteria and exceptions; obtain a recent certificate from a named Tamil Nadu medical board and confirm your case with the Committee. The general above-80% exclusion and the annexure’s case-by-case assistive-device exception differ; obtain the competent medical-board decision rather than choosing between them yourself.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Disability-specific functional criteria
rules.explanation: For medical-course eligibility the prospectus says both hands must be intact, with intact sensations, sufficient strength and range of motion. Annexure II sets disability-specific criteria for locomotor, visual, hearing, speech/language, intellectual, mental-behavioural, neurological, blood-disorder and multiple disabilities. These require a manual board assessment; see Annexure II and confirm conflicting or case-by-case criteria with the Committee.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Nationality wording needs confirmation
rules.explanation: Clause 5(i) says candidates should be citizens of India. The next clause says Indian nationals, OCI card holders, Persons with Indian Origin and foreign nationals are eligible for admission subject to State, institutional and Government of India rules. Confirm the applicable nationality rule with the Selection Committee; the prospectus does not reconcile these statements. Clause 5(ii)(b) separately says OCI holders retain rights and privileges conferred before the notification dated 4th March 2021, in compliance with the Supreme Court order dated 3rd February 2023; confirm the eligible quota/category route with the authority.
rules.note: Conflicting clauses; do not automatically exclude OCI or foreign-national candidates from this prospectus.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: NEET PG 2026 qualification
rules.explanation: Candidates must qualify NEET PG 2026 conducted by the National Board of Examination; the prospectus says the applicable national eligibility criteria also apply.
rules.note: The profile has no NEET qualification or score field.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: General-category qualifying threshold
rules.explanation: The prospectus table lists General candidates at the 50th percentile, score 262 out of 800. A later Tamil Nadu-specific paragraph also states a 50th-percentile minimum for General candidates.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Reserved-category qualifying threshold and Tamil Nadu nativity wording
rules.explanation: The table lists SC / ST / OBC candidates, including persons with disability, at the 40th percentile and score 226. The Tamil Nadu-specific paragraph says the 40th-percentile threshold applies to Tamil Nadu natives in SC, SC (Arunthathiyar), ST, BC, BC (Muslim), MBC and Denotified Communities. The prospectus does not define a profile-mappable test for its word “natives.”
rules.note: Do not substitute domicile, birthplace or study history for the prospectus's undefined “native” test.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: General-category candidates with disability qualifying threshold
rules.explanation: The table lists General-Persons with Disabilities at the 45th percentile and score 244 out of 800; the Tamil Nadu-specific paragraph also states a 45th-percentile minimum for General-category candidates with disabilities.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: CRMI / CRRI deadline
rules.explanation: Candidates must have cleared MBBS and completed, or be completing, CRMI / CRRI on or before 30th September 2026.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Medical registration certificate
rules.explanation: Candidates must have a permanent or provisional Medical Council registration certificate from a State Medical Council or India at counselling / admission.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Recognized MBBS degree and Tamil Nadu eligibility certificate
rules.explanation: Candidates must hold an MBBS degree awarded by The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University or another university recognized by the Medical Council of India. A candidate qualified from another university must obtain the Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University eligibility certificate and submit it with the application.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Who may seek NRI quota
rules.explanation: The prospectus lists these NRI-quota candidate routes: a person of Indian origin settled in a foreign country; a person born in a foreign country whose parents are of Indian origin; a child of an Indian citizen staying abroad for employment or business; a child of an Indian citizen deputed abroad by a public sector undertaking; or a child of a Central / State Government official deputed abroad.
rules.note: The listed routes do not map fully to existing profile facts; verify the exact route manually.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: NRI-quota passport / OCI requirement
rules.explanation: A candidate seeking NRI quota must have a valid Indian passport or OCI card. Clause 16 also lists the OCI card of the sponsor or candidate among the documents.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Permitted NRI financial supporter
rules.explanation: NRI quota seats are for bona fide NRIs and their children or wards. The financial supporter must be the candidate's father or mother, spouse, a blood relative, or a guardian legally declared by a Court under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890. The source does not state a separate “parents absent” exception.
rules.note: Sponsor relationship and court-declared guardianship cannot be fully checked with current profile facts.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Blood-relative sponsor definition
rules.explanation: For this prospectus, a blood relative must be one of the following permitted relationships: the candidate's father's real brother or sister (real uncle or aunt); mother's real brother or sister (maternal uncle or aunt); father's parents; mother's parents; or a first-degree paternal or maternal cousin. The person must be an NRI.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: NRI selection basis wording
rules.explanation: The prospectus says admission under the NRI scheme “may be made” on the basis of marks obtained in the qualifying examination “as prescribed.” It does not define this phrase here.
rules.note: Preserve the source's “may”; the passage does not say this is the exclusive selection basis.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Currently undergoing a postgraduate course
rules.explanation: Candidates currently undergoing a Postgraduate Degree, DNB, equivalent or Diploma course are not eligible to apply for any Postgraduate Degree / Diploma course.
rules.note: The profile's currentlyInPG field is narrower than the source's broad wording; leave manual rather than using it as a proxy.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Already completed a postgraduate course
rules.explanation: Candidates who have already completed a Postgraduate Degree, DNB or equivalent course are not eligible to apply for another Postgraduate Degree / Diploma course.
rules.note: No profile fact records all prior postgraduate qualifications.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Already holds a Diploma
rules.explanation: A candidate who already holds a Diploma cannot apply for another Diploma course, but can apply for any Postgraduate Degree course.
rules.note: The profile does not record prior Diploma qualifications.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Diploma candidates applying for a postgraduate degree
rules.explanation: The prospectus says PG Degree courses generally last three years. Candidates pursuing a Diploma course, including through All India Quota, may apply for a Postgraduate Degree in the same academic year if they complete the Diploma before counselling begins (identified in the prospectus as the date of notification of the online application). A two-year Diploma holder's postgraduate degree duration is two years in the same specialty and three years in another specialty. This concession does not apply after a one-year Diploma; Diploma in Clinical Pathology and Diploma in Diabetology lead to a three-year postgraduate degree. All Diploma courses last two years.
rules.note: The source links counselling commencement to the online-application notification date; it does not state a separate clock time for Diploma completion.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: False NRI documents
rules.explanation: If NRI documents are found false, the prospectus says criminal action will be initiated whether or not the candidate was allotted a seat. An allotment based on false documents will be cancelled; the candidate will not be allotted under any category, will be debarred for three years, and will receive no refund of security deposit or tuition fee paid.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Suppressed or misrepresented eligibility information
rules.explanation: The prospectus states that suppressing or hiding an eligibility or non-eligibility criterion will result in cancellation of the allotment order and appropriate legal / disciplinary action. If suppression is found later, selection / admission is liable for cancellation; candidates give a self-declaration at reporting that selection / admission is liable for forfeiture if suppression or misinterpretation is found.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB applicants must meet the NEET-PG 2026 percentile stated for their category
rules.explanation: The prospectus requires NEET-PG 2026 qualification. It states a 50th-percentile minimum for General candidates; a 40th-percentile minimum for Tamil Nadu natives in SC, SCA, ST, BC, BCM, MBC or DNC communities; a 40th-percentile minimum for SC-PH, ST-PH and OBC-PH candidates; and a 45th-percentile minimum for General-PH candidates.
rules.note: Manual DNB check: the profile has no DNB subtype and cannot distinguish BC, BCM, MBC, DNC or SCA as used by Tamil Nadu. The score-out-of-800 columns in the p.98 table are blank; only percentile thresholds in p.99 are stated.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB citizenship, Tamil Nadu MBBS and nativity clauses need a manual eligibility check
rules.explanation: Clause 5(b) says candidates must be Indian citizens and must have completed the MBBS course, including the entire CRMI/CRRI internship, in Tamil Nadu. Clause 5(c) also directs candidates claiming Tamil Nadu nativity after completing MBBS in another state to upload a Tamil Nadu Nativity Certificate. Clause 10(b) says candidates belonging to other states are not eligible. The prospectus does not say whether the nativity route in Clause 5(c) is an exception to the Tamil Nadu MBBS and internship requirement in Clause 5(b).
rules.note: Source tension at merged pp.98-100 (original pp.7-9): Clause 5(b) requires Tamil Nadu MBBS plus the entire internship in Tamil Nadu, while Clause 5(c) addresses Tamil Nadu natives who completed MBBS outside Tamil Nadu. Clause 10(b) separately excludes candidates belonging to other states. Do not choose an interpretation without Selection Committee confirmation.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Dual nativity found can cancel the allotment
rules.explanation: The prospectus advises against dual nativity. If dual nativity is found at any time during admission or the course, the allotment will be cancelled and appropriate legal action would be initiated by competent authorities.
rules.note: Manual DNB check: the profile has no Tamil Nadu nativity-certificate or dual-nativity fact; the source uses 'would be initiated' for legal action.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Tamil Nadu community reservation requires candidate and parent certificates
rules.explanation: Candidates claiming Tamil Nadu community reservation must upload their community certificate issued by the competent Tamil Nadu Revenue and Disaster Management authority with official seal, and a community certificate for either one parent issued by that authority with official seal. The prospectus identifies BC, BCM, MBC, DNC, SC and SCA groups; ST certificates are issued by the competent Revenue Divisional Officer.
rules.note: Manual DNB check: the profile's category field cannot distinguish all Tamil Nadu community groups or certificate routes. The current profile's OBC value is not a verified mapping for BC, BCM, MBC, DNC or SCA.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Quota seats are limited to eligible in-service candidates
rules.explanation: The prospectus says only in-service candidates may apply for the DNB State Quota. It defines qualifying routes in Clause 12: specified TNPSC/MRB appointees in Tamil Nadu Medical Services, or Medical Officers serving in Tamil Nadu Local Bodies, subject to the stated continuous-service requirement. Registered Societies Act and self-financing institution employees are treated as non-service candidates.
rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB service-candidate status depends on the specified appointment route
rules.explanation: Eligible routes are Medical Officers selected by TNPSC or MRB through a Competitive Written Examination or Special Qualifying Examination and appointed in Tamil Nadu Medical Services, with at least two years of continuous service as at 31st March 2026; or Medical Officers serving in Tamil Nadu Local Bodies, also with at least two years of continuous service as at 31st March 2026.
rules.note: Manual DNB check: the profile's inServiceListed boolean is reliable only if its question uses these exact appointment routes and service dates; employment by Tamil Nadu alone is not enough.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Some temporary DNB service appointments are excluded
rules.explanation: Clause 12(b) says temporarily appointed candidates who have not completed two years of continuous service as at 31st March 2026, as per Clause 12(a)(i), are not eligible for 2026-2027 PG admission; even an application inadvertently certified by the competent authority will be summarily rejected.
rules.note: Manual DNB check. The source cross-reference specifically cites Clause 12(a)(i), although Clause 12(a)(ii) separately describes Local Body Medical Officers; do not extend this sentence beyond its wording.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB staff at specified institutions do not count as service candidates
rules.explanation: Candidates working in institutions under the Registered Societies Act or in self-financing institutions are considered non-service candidates for this DNB prospectus.
rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Quota service candidates need more than five years of service after training
rules.explanation: Clause 12 requires at least five years of left-over service on course completion. Clause 33(d) says Tamil Nadu service candidates should have more than five years of service after course completion and must serve the Government until superannuation.
rules.note: Manual DNB check: the profile has no service-retirement date. The source uses both 'minimum Five years' (Clause 12) and 'more than 5 years' (Clause 26(d)); treatment of exactly five years is unresolved.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB applicants must disclose Government or Local Body employment
rules.explanation: A Medical Officer working in a Government institution or Local Body who applies as a private candidate while suppressing service status will have the application summarily rejected and any allotment cancelled if the status is found later.
rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Prior PG degree or DNB qualification bars another DNB seat under this prospectus
rules.explanation: Candidates who have already completed a Post Graduate Degree, DNB or equivalent course are not eligible to apply for any other DNB Broad Specialty (Post MBBS) or Post MBBS Diploma seat in 2026-2027.
rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Some current diploma candidates may apply for DNB in the same academic year

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB applicants need MBBS and CRMI/CRRI completion by 30th September 2026
rules.explanation: Only candidates who have cleared the MBBS examination and completed or are completing CRMI/CRRI on or before 30th September 2026 may apply. rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB applicants need a recognized MBBS degree and some need a Tamil Nadu MGR University certificate

A candidate who qualified from another university must produce an eligibility certificate from Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University, Guindy, Chennai, at counselling/admission.
rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB eligibility or non-eligibility facts must not be hidden
rules.explanation: Suppressing or hiding eligibility/non-eligibility criteria will result in cancellation of allotment, and appropriate legal/disciplinary action will be taken. Clause 19 separately makes selection/admission liable to forfeiture if suppression or misinterpretation is found during or after admission. Clause 20 applies cancellation and the subsequent-two-academic-year DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma application bar when suppression of facts is found later; it does not expressly attach that bar to misinterpretation alone.
rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB NEET-PG eligibility also follows current NBEMS admission criteria

rules.note: Manual check: the profile does not identify DNB versus other clinical courses, so this DNB-only rule must not be applied automatically to every clinical applicant.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Confirm disability ranges and the above-80% exception
rules.explanation: The general clause says candidates with 40–80% disability may be considered eligible; above 80% is stated ineligible for admission; below 40% is ineligible for PwD reservation but may apply under General Category. The locomotor matrix separately permits some above-80% cases after assistive-device and functional assessment. These passages differ; obtain the competent board decision and confirm the operative PG criteria.

manualReview.title: Confirm the requirements for your quota and programme
manualReview.detail: The profile cannot establish all eligibility requirements in these prospectuses. Check every manual rule for the quota and programme you seek before applying. Source wording conflicts are identified where found and need confirmation with the Selection Committee. A profile result alone cannot confirm eligibility; DNB-only criteria apply only when seeking those DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma seats.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Government Medical College seat split
rules.detail: Of recognized/permitted postgraduate Diploma and degree seats sanctioned in Government Medical Colleges, 50% are offered to All India Quota for DGHS allotment and the remaining 50% are allotted under State Quota.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Service and Open category State seats
rules.detail: The prospectus says that of the seats in State Government quota, 50% are exclusively for in-service candidates serving in Tamil Nadu Government health institutions and 50% are Open category seats available to both service and non-service candidates. Allotment uses the marks/criteria defined by the Government or the committee described in the prospectus.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Rural-service Diploma allocation
rules.detail: The prospectus reserves 50% of postgraduate Diploma seats for Government medical officers who have served at least three years in hilly, remote, difficult or rural areas of Tamil Nadu. After acquiring the Diploma, those officers must serve two more years in such areas as defined by the State Government/competent authority.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Reservation roster by specialty seat count
rules.detail: The prospectus says the Tamil Nadu 200-point roster is followed if a specialty has more than one and fewer than eight seats. If exactly one seat is available in a specialty, allotment is by rank alone. If eight or more seats are available, the published community percentages apply. The roster clause is subject to the final verdict in its cited court proceedings. The court-reference passage is garbled and prints “Supreme Madras” with Civil Appeal Nos.6049–6050/2010, W.A. Nos.763 and 764/2007, W.P. No.7067/2009 and 12th May 2009. Confirm the operative court/roster position with the Selection Committee.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Backward Class Muslim sub-reservation
rules.detail: Within the 30% Backward Class reservation, 3.5% reservation is provided for Backward Class Muslims. If no eligible BCM candidates are available after the merit list is exhausted, remaining BCM seats are filled by BC candidates on merit without exceeding the BC quota overall.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Scheduled Caste (Arunthathiyar) allocation
rules.detail: Sixteen percent of the seats out of the 18% quota earmarked for Scheduled Castes are allocated to Scheduled Caste (Arunthathiyar). If eligible SCA candidates are unavailable, remaining seats go to SC candidates by merit. Qualified SCA candidates in excess of the preferential seats may compete with other SC candidates by inter-se merit.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Unfilled Scheduled Tribe seats
rules.detail: If eligible ST candidates are unavailable for reserved ST seats, the remaining seats are filled by SC candidates on merit; SC candidates may register and choice-lock for those seats.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: No eligible service candidates
rules.detail: If no eligible service candidates opt for PG degree/Diploma courses, those seats are allotted to eligible General category candidates.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: PwD seat order and conversion
rules.detail: PwD special-category allotment is done ahead of General category according to the schedule. There is no reallotment/change of college for a special-category allotment. If adequate eligible candidates are unavailable, or a special-category seat is discontinued/not joined, the seat is returned to General category.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Government Quota seat sharing in Self-Financing colleges
rules.detail: Seat sharing with Self-Financing Minority and Non-Minority Medical Colleges is according to State policy, NMC Postgraduate Medical Education Regulations and applicable court orders. The prospectus does not list the resulting college/course seat counts.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Tamil Nadu community categories
rules.detail: The prospectus uses BC, BC Muslim, MBC, Denotified Community, SC, SCA and ST categories. Annexure pages list the communities and location-specific qualifications. The profile has no separate fields for BC vs BCM vs MBC/DNC or SC vs SCA; verify the certificate and roster category manually.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Management seats in minority and non-minority colleges
rules.detail: Seat sharing between self-financing minority and non-minority colleges is to follow State Policy, MCI Post Graduate Medical Education Regulations and applicable Court Orders. This prospectus gives no numerical minority allocation or priority order.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: NRI quota share
rules.detail: Up to 15% of total sanctioned seats among Management Quota seats will be allotted for NRI quota, citing Supreme Court civil appeals and the Nilay Gupta matter.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Unfilled NRI seats
rules.detail: Unfilled NRI quota seats revert to Management Quota.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Rank and reservation in online counselling
rules.detail: Admission is through online counselling by rank with the rule of reservation. Re-allotment is permitted only in Round 2 and is based on rank and the rule of reservation.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Quota selection follows rank, Tamil Nadu reservation and a 200-point roster
rules.detail: Selection is based on the merit list with the Tamil Nadu Rule of Reservation / 200-point roster method wherever applicable. If more than one and fewer than eight seats are available in each branch, the 200-point roster is used. If one seat is available in a specialty, it is allotted by rank only. The roster clause is subject to the final Supreme Court verdict in the cited civil appeal; confirm the operative roster notice.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Quota category shares apply at eight or more seats in a specialty
rules.detail: For eight or more seats, the prospectus lists Open Competition 31%, BC 30%, MBC/DNC 20%, SC 18% and ST 1%. Within BC, 3.5% is reserved for Backward Class Muslims. The prospectus says 16% of seats out of the 18% quota earmarked for SC are allocated to the Scheduled Caste (Arunthathiyar) community.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB PwD special-category seats are listed as 5% of Government Medical Institution seats
rules.detail: The prospectus reserves 5% of the total seats available in Government Medical Institutions for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. PwD Special Category allotment is conducted before General Category allotment and cannot be re-allotted to another college. The prospectus does not clarify whether the 5% denominator is the State Quota half or all recognised Government Institution seats; confirm the operative seat count.
rules.note: The source says 'total number of seats available in Government Medical Institutions' and does not state whether this 5% applies to the State Quota half or all recognized seats. Confirm the seat-count basis with the Selection Committee.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB unfilled or discontinued PwD seats move to General Category
rules.detail: If enough eligible candidates are not available in the PwD Special Category, earmarked seats revert to General Category. A candidate cannot remain on the waiting list when a seat is available in their specialty. Discontinued or not-joined Special Category vacancies are added to General Category.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB unfilled SCA seats may be chosen by SC candidates
rules.detail: The prospectus says SCA seats may be filled by SC candidates on merit and expressly states SC candidates may register and choice-lock remaining unfilled SCA seats. The clause also says 'vice versa'; it does not clearly describe the reverse direction.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB unfilled ST seats may be filled by SC candidates
rules.detail: Where eligible ST candidates are insufficient, remaining ST quota seats may be filled by SC candidates on merit. SC candidates may register and choice-lock remaining unfilled ST seats.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB unfilled BCM seats shall be filled by BC candidates within the BC total
rules.detail: After the BCM merit list is exhausted, remaining BCM seats shall be filled on merit by BC candidates, without exceeding the BC quota as a whole. BC candidates may register and choice-lock remaining unfilled BCM seats.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB excess qualified SCA candidates may compete within the other SC merit list
rules.detail: After the seats reserved for Arunthathiyars are filled on a preferential basis, any excess qualified Arunthathiyar candidates may compete with SC candidates other than Arunthathiyars in their inter-se merit.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB seats may revert to General Category when no eligible PwD candidate opts
rules.detail: If no eligible PwD candidates opt for DNB Broad Specialty or Post MBBS Diploma seats, the prospectus says those seats will be allotted to eligible General Category candidates.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Quota reservation
rules.detail: DNB State Quota selection in Government Medical Colleges and Government Hospitals. The vertical shares apply when there are 8 or more seats in a specialty. The prospectus separately describes 5% PwD seats as a share of total seats in Government Medical Institutions, without clarifying whether that is across both quota halves. Shares: Open Competition 31%; Backward Classes (BC) 30%; Most Backward Classes / Denotified Communities (MBC/DNC) 20%; Scheduled Caste (SC) 18%; Scheduled Tribe (ST) 1%. PwD: 5%, with the denominator and assessment qualifications stated in the DNB rules.
rules.note: Tamil Nadu categories BC, BCM, MBC, DNC and SCA do not map cleanly to the current profile's generic category values; manual review is required.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB reserved-seat fall-through
rules.detail: DNB State Quota reservation when a reserved or special-category seat remains unfilled for lack of eligible candidates, subject to cited Government Orders. PwD Special Category → General Category; SCA → SC (remaining unfilled SCA seats may be chosen by SC candidates); ST → SC; BCM → BC, without exceeding the total BC quota. The SCA “vice versa” wording is unclear; confirm the reverse route with the Selection Committee.
rules.note: Clause 30(g) says SCA seats are filled by SC candidates 'vice versa', then expressly says SC candidates can choose remaining unfilled SCA seats. The reverse direction is unclear.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 1 counselling registration fee
rules.detail: Candidates participating in Round 1 must pay ₹1,000 online as a non-refundable counselling registration fee.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 counselling registration fee
rules.detail: The Round 3 registration fee is ₹1,000. Candidates allotted and not joined/resigned earlier, and fresh Round 3 registrants, must pay it. Only candidates not allotted in both Round 1 and Round 2 need not pay.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Stray Vacancy Round registration fee
rules.detail: The Stray Vacancy Round registration fee is ₹1,000. Candidates allotted and not joined/resigned in Round 1 or Round 2, and fresh registrants, must pay. Only candidates not allotted in Rounds 1, 2 or 3 need not pay.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Security-deposit refund
rules.detail: The deposit is refunded to candidates who could not get any seat in any phase of counselling, within three months after the entire counselling process ends. No interest is paid. The prospectus says the deposit is not refunded in the circumstances in clause 27(b)(ii), which covers a Round 3 allotment not joined. It does not define every candidate who is an eligible refund recipient.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Government Medical College fees
rules.detail: The printed 2026-2027 annual non-refundable fees are: PG Diploma tuition ₹20,000; PG Degree tuition ₹40,000 plus special fee ₹10,000. Candidates must pay through online RTGS/Demand Draft, subject to realization, and any balance tuition or other special fees at admission. Eligible differently abled candidates are exempt from tuition and special fees in Government Medical Institutions under the cited Government Orders.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Government Quota fees in Self-Financing colleges
rules.detail: Fees for 2026-2027 are set by the Committee on Fixation of Fees in Respect of Self-Financing Professional Colleges; this prospectus gives no amount. The selected candidate must pay the full tuition and special fees online when downloading the allotment order. The Committee handles grievances about fees collected by the institutions.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Online payment and failed transactions
rules.detail: Payments use the online portal and the stated options include Debit/Credit Card, Net Banking, UPI and RTGS; the Government-institution fee text also names Demand Draft, subject to realization. A bank deduction alone is not proof of payment. Candidates must check limits/funds and pay before closing time; the Selection Committee disclaims responsibility for banking-system failures or insufficient funds.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Stipend and salary
rules.detail: Non-service candidates in Government Medical Colleges receive stipend under current Government Orders and institution norms. Service candidates in Government Medical Colleges receive salary under Government Orders. The prospectus gives no fixed stipend or salary amount. Non-service candidates, including the 50% All India Quota candidates, are paid stipend only until age 60.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Application fee payment
rules.detail: The ₹5,000 application fee is non-refundable and paid online. The prospectus lists debit card, credit card, net banking, RTGS and UPI; a bank debit alone is not proof of payment. Check card validity and transaction limits before paying, and avoid a last-minute rush.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 1 counselling registration fee
rules.detail: Candidates participating in online counselling pay a non-refundable ₹1,000 registration fee online for Round 1.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 registration fee
rules.detail: Round 3 registration is ₹1,000. Candidates allotted and not joined or resigned, and candidates freshly registering, must pay; candidates not allotted in Rounds 1 and 2 need not pay.
rules.note: The text does not clearly say whether a candidate who joined and still holds a Round 1 / 2 seat pays this fee; the listed pay cases are non-joining / resignation and fresh registration, while the exemption names only candidates not allotted in Rounds 1 and 2.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Stray Vacancy Round registration fee
rules.detail: Stray Vacancy Round registration is ₹1,000. Candidates allotted and not joined / resigned within the stipulated time in Rounds 1 or 2, and fresh registrants, must pay. Candidates not allotted in Rounds 1, 2 and 3 need not pay.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Security deposit refund when no seat is allotted
rules.detail: If a candidate gets no seat in any counselling phase, the security deposit is refunded within three months after the entire counselling process ends. No interest is paid.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Security deposit forfeiture after later-round non-joining
rules.detail: The round tables say candidates allotted in Round 3 or Stray who do not join forfeit the registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee paid. See the resignation ladder for the round-by-round consequences.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Tuition and special fees
rules.detail: The Fee Fixation Committee sets 2026–2027 fees for Management Quota including NRI seats in self-financing institutions. The selected candidate must pay the full tuition and special fees online when downloading the allotment order; the tuition fee is non-refundable. Any grievance about excess fees charged by a self-financing institution must be represented only to the Fee Fixation Committee. Listed payment methods are Net Banking, RTGS, debit card, credit card and UPI. Ensure a sufficient transaction limit and funds, avoid last-minute payment, and complete payment well before the closing time. The Selection Committee disclaims responsibility for failures from banking technical issues or insufficient funds.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Discontinuation fees after joining
rules.detail: Candidates who discontinue after the Selection Committee's resignation period must forfeit tuition paid and pay ₹10,00,000 for a PG Diploma or ₹15,00,000 for a PG Degree. The prospectus says the amount is paid to the Dean of the respective college by a demand draft drawn in favour of the Secretary, Selection Committee, Kilpauk, Chennai–10, payable at Chennai; until paid in full, the candidate will not be relieved and the college retains original certificates. Clause 11 calls one forfeited charge “processing fee”, while later clauses/tables say “registration fee”; confirm whether these names refer to the same charge.
rules.note: Clause 27(vi) separately says “State Quota candidates”; this item relies on the general Clause 25 and the counselling tables, and does not extend that State Quota-only sentence to MQ/NRI.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: No refund for false NRI documents
rules.detail: For false NRI documents, the prospectus states that tuition fee and security deposit will not be refunded; the NRI definition clause also says no refund of fees paid.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB counselling registration costs ₹1,000 and is non-refundable
rules.detail: Candidates must pay a non-refundable ₹1,000 online registration-cum-processing fee for counselling. Round 3 and Stray Round also state ₹1,000 fees with the exemptions stated in their rules.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB security deposit is refunded after counselling without interest
rules.detail: The ₹30,000 security deposit for Government Institutions/Hospitals is to be refunded within three months after the entire counselling process ends. No interest is paid on the deposit.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB tuition and special fees are payable at admission
rules.detail: Selected candidates pay tuition and other special fees at admission to their institution. This prospectus does not state the amounts; it says candidates will be guided by a later website notification.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Eligible differently abled DNB candidates have a tuition and special-fee exemption
rules.detail: The prospectus cites G.O. (Ms.) No. 135 dated 20th September 2008 and G.O. (Ms.) No. 30 dated 28th June 2010 and says eligible differently abled candidates are exempt from tuition and special fees during NEET-PG counselling/admission in Government Medical Institutions.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: A bank debit alone is not proof of payment
rules.detail: Fees are paid through the online portal. A bank deduction alone is not proof of payment; check card/banking/UPI transaction limits before making payment.

rules.title: MD/MS/Diploma in Government colleges: All India Quota discontinuation clause
rules.detail: For All India Quota candidates, clause 24(b) says discontinuation on or after the date stipulated by AIQ counselling requires payment of the printed discontinuation fee and forfeiture of tuition already paid. The fee table gives ₹10,00,000 for PG Diploma and ₹15,00,000 for PG Degree. Payment is to the Dean by a demand draft drawn in favour of the Secretary, Selection Committee, Kilpauk, Chennai–10, payable at Chennai. The non-relief/original-certificate retention sentence follows the State Quota paragraph; its application to AIQ is not explicit, so confirm that consequence with the institution. This is the AIQ-specific clause, separate from the State Quota resignation trigger.
