choiceFilling.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Online choice and allotment
choiceFilling.detail: Admission is by online counselling, rank and Tamil Nadu reservation/roster. Follow the current counselling notice for choice-filling, choice-locking and deadlines.

choiceFilling.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 reallotment
choiceFilling.detail: Reallotment is permitted in Round 2 only, based on rank and the rule of reservation. A Round 1 allotment held for upgradation is shown as a virtual vacancy in Round 2; another candidate may choose it, but it becomes a real vacancy only if the Round 1 candidate vacates it, after which it is open by merit.

choiceFilling.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: No college transfers
choiceFilling.detail: Mutual transfer and individual requests to transfer colleges are not permitted under any circumstances.

choiceFilling.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Choose only seats you are prepared to join
choiceFilling.detail: The prospectus advises candidates not to list unwanted seats. If a Government College/Government Quota seat in a Self-Financing college is allotted in State Round 3, the candidate cannot claim a seat in the Management Round 3 counselling.

choiceFilling.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Online choices and allotment
choiceFilling.detail: Admission is through online counselling by rank and the rule of reservation. Candidates download the allotment order and join by its stated deadline.

choiceFilling.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: No mutual transfer or individual transfer request
choiceFilling.detail: Mutual transfer and individual requests to transfer colleges are not permitted under any circumstances.

choiceFilling.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Re-allotment only in Round 2
choiceFilling.detail: Re-allotment is permitted only during Round 2, based on rank and the rule of reservation.

choiceFilling.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 virtual vacancies
choiceFilling.detail: A Round 1 allottee opting for re-allotment has their Round 1 seat shown as a virtual vacancy in Round 2. Others may lock that choice, but it is allotted only if the Round 1 candidate vacates it; it then becomes a real vacancy open by merit order.

choiceFilling.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB choices are allotted online by rank and reservation
choiceFilling.detail: Admission to DNB Broad Specialty and Post MBBS Diploma seats is through online counselling based on rank and the Rule of Reservation. Mutual transfer or an individual request to transfer colleges is not permitted under any circumstances.

choiceFilling.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB candidates who miss Round 1 registration can enter later rounds
choiceFilling.detail: An applicant who skipped registration and choice-locking in the first round may participate in later online counselling rounds. Someone allotted a Round 1 seat who did not join or resigned within the stipulated period may participate in Round 2.

choiceFilling.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB re-allotment is available only in Rounds 2 and 3
choiceFilling.detail: Re-allotment is permitted during Round 2 and Round 3 only, based on rank and the Rule of Reservation.

choiceFilling.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB upgradation seats may appear as virtual vacancies
choiceFilling.detail: A Round 1 seat held by a candidate who opts for Round 2 upgradation may be shown as a virtual vacancy and can be filled in Round 2 choices. It is allotted only if the Round 1 candidate vacates it; then it becomes a real vacancy open by merit. The same rule applies to Round 2 upgradation.

choiceFilling.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB candidates should lock only seats they are prepared to join
choiceFilling.detail: The prospectus says candidates should join the institution if a seat is allotted according to their choices and should be vigilant while choice-filling.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Four rounds are described
rounds.detail: The prospectus provides Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 and a Stray Vacancy Round. It says DGHS-notified changes to the counselling procedure will also apply to State counselling; exact schedules are announced later.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 1 participation and exit
rounds.detail: Round 1 candidates pay ₹1,000 registration fee. Free exit is allowed, and resignation is allowed within the date/time set by the Selection Committee. A Round 1 candidate who has not registered and has not choice-locked may participate in later rounds; an allotted candidate who does not join or resigns within the stipulated time may participate in Round 2. A candidate who joins may participate in Round 2 for reallotment.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 vacancies and choices
rounds.detail: Round 2 fills vacancies from not-joined, not-allotted and resigned seats, and newly sanctioned seats arising after Round 1, by rank and community reservation. Candidates not registered and not choice-locked in Round 1 and candidates allotted but not joined or resigned in time in the first round may participate. Reallotment occurs only in Round 2 and is based on rank and reservation.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 exit, resignation and later eligibility
rounds.detail: Candidates retaining a Round 1 seat beyond the stated date, newly allotted in Round 2 or reallotted in the second round may vacate within the date set by the Selection Committee; candidates who joined in the second round may resign within the stipulated date. A Round 2 allottee who does not download the allotment order and join after Round 2 ends forfeits the registration fee. Resigning after the Round 2 deadline makes the candidate ineligible for Round 3 and later rounds and triggers the stated discontinuation fee and forfeiture of registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Who may participate in Round 3
rounds.detail: The detailed eligibility list includes candidates not allotted in Rounds 1 and 2; candidates allotted, joined or not joined in Rounds 1 or 2 of State or All India Quota; candidates who did not register and did not choice-lock in Rounds 1 and 2; and candidates who joined a State Round 1/2 seat but resigned in Round 2 within the stipulated date. Candidates allotted in All India Round 3 are blocked if MCC shares their joined list with the State before State Round 3 results. Page 19 describes Round 1/2 allottees who have joined, while page 20 lists “Joined / not joined” candidates in State or All India Rounds 1 and 2. These clauses differ: confirm your exact earlier-round status with the Selection Committee before Round 3.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 fee and finality
rounds.detail: Round 3 registration is ₹1,000 for candidates allotted and not joined/resigned earlier and for fresh registrants; candidates not allotted in both Rounds 1 and 2 do not pay. Any candidate allotted a State Round 3 seat is ineligible for later rounds. If the candidate does not join, they forfeit the registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee, whether or not the allotment order was downloaded. The prospectus table also says a Round 3 joined/upgraded seat cannot be vacated; a candidate seeking to discontinue after joining forfeits those amounts and pays the discontinuation fee.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Who may participate in the Stray Vacancy Round
rounds.detail: Eligible candidates include those not allotted in State Rounds 1–3; candidates allotted but not joined in State or All India Rounds 1 or 2; and candidates who did not register and did not choice-lock in Rounds 1, 2 or 3. Candidates holding a State PG seat in Rounds 1–3, holding an All India/Deemed/DNB seat in Rounds 1–3, or allotted an All India stray seat are excluded. A candidate allotted in State Round 3 and not joined cannot participate in a further round. A Stray allotment in All India Quota, a Deemed University or DNB also excludes the candidate from State Stray counselling, as stated on page 21. The fee paragraph mentions “not joined / resigned”, while the eligible list does not expressly include timely resigned candidates. Confirm that eligibility with the Selection Committee.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Stray Vacancy Round fee and compulsory joining
rounds.detail: The Stray Vacancy Round fee is ₹1,000 for previously allotted and not joined/resigned candidates and for fresh registrants; only candidates not allotted in Rounds 1, 2 or 3 do not pay. Because it is a stray round, a candidate allotted a seat according to their choices must join without fail.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Stray Vacancy Round seat consequences
rounds.detail: The prospectus table says a candidate allotted but not joined forfeits registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee. A joined Stray seat cannot be vacated; a candidate who discontinues after joining forfeits those amounts and pays the discontinuation fee. No later round is described for such a candidate.

rounds.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Any further round
rounds.detail: The prospectus says any further counselling round directed by DGHS may be conducted. No dates or eligibility details are provided.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Four planned counselling rounds
rounds.detail: The prospectus lists Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 and Stray Round. It says the scheme is subject to DGHS / MCC guidelines and Court orders; further rounds may be held if directed by DGHS.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 1 participation and exit
rounds.detail: Candidates who do not register and choice-lock in the first round may attend later rounds. A Round 1 candidate who takes a seat, does not join, or resigns within the stipulated time may attend Round 2. Round 1 candidates allotted and joined may participate in Round 2 for re-allotment. Round 1 allotted candidates must download the order and join by the stated deadline.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 vacancies and exit window
rounds.detail: Round 2 fills vacancies from non-joining, non-allotment, resignation and newly sanctioned seats, by rank. Candidates who retained a Round 1 seat beyond its deadline, received re-allotment, or were newly allotted in the second round may vacate within the date set by the Selection Committee. Round 2 joined candidates may resign within that stated period.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 eligibility
rounds.detail: Candidates who did not register and choice-lock in the first round may attend Round 2. Candidates who took a Round 1 seat, did not join, or resigned within the stipulated time may attend Round 2. The table expressly permits a Round 1 candidate who was not allotted a seat to participate in subsequent rounds.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 eligibility
rounds.detail: The prospectus lists as eligible: candidates not allotted in Rounds 1 and 2; candidates allotted and joined / not joined in Round 1 or Round 2 of State Quota and All India Quota; candidates who did not register and choice-lock in Round 1 or 2; and candidates who joined a State counselling seat in Round 1 or 2 but resigned within the stipulated Round 2 time. If MCC sends the joined list for a candidate allotted in All India Round 3, that candidate is blocked before State Round 3 results display.
rounds.note: Round history and MCC joined-list status are not profile facts; manual check.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 disqualification after late Round 2 resignation
rounds.detail: Candidates who resign after the stipulated date and time following Round 2 are not eligible for Round 3.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 allotment and non-joining
rounds.detail: A candidate allotted in State Round 3 is ineligible for further rounds. If allotted but not joined, the candidate forfeits registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee paid whether or not the allotment order was downloaded. If the candidate joins and later discontinues, the tables state that forfeitures and discontinuation fees apply. Clause 11(b) separately says a candidate who downloaded a Round 3 allotment order must join; otherwise the candidate is considered discontinued and must pay the discontinuation fee. Confirm the operative fee consequence with the Selection Committee when the order was not downloaded.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Stray Round eligibility and exclusions
rounds.detail: Eligible candidates include those not allotted through Round 3; candidates allotted but not joined in Round 1 or Round 2 of State or All India counselling; and candidates who did not register and choice-lock in Rounds 1, 2 or 3. The prospectus excludes candidates holding a PG seat in State counselling Rounds 1–3; candidates holding All India, Deemed University or DNB seats in Rounds 1–3; candidates allotted an All India Stray seat; and candidates allotted a State Round 3 seat who did not join. A candidate discontinued with penalty after the stipulated time cannot participate further. The registration-fee clause mentions allotted candidates who “not joined / resigned” in Rounds 1 or 2, while the eligible list mentions allotted-but-not-joined candidates without expressly naming timely resignations. Confirm with the Selection Committee whether a timely resigned candidate is eligible.
rounds.note: These exclusions depend on seat history across State, All India, Deemed, DNB and Stray rounds and cannot be computed from current profile facts.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Stray Round allotment must be joined
rounds.detail: Because this is a Stray Vacancy Round, a candidate allotted a PG seat according to their choices should join without fail.

rounds.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Cross-round table: re-allotted but not joined
rounds.detail: The cross-round table has a separate “If Re-allotted and not joined” row: it says the candidate cannot vacate the seat, must pay the discontinuation fee, and forfeits tuition and security deposit; it marks the candidate not eligible for further rounds. The table does not make clear which round’s re-allotment this row addresses.
rounds.note: Manual review due to table placement and wording.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Rank List is based on NEET-PG 2026 marks
rounds.detail: The State Rank List is drawn based on marks obtained in NEET-PG 2026. Provisional Rank Lists are published at tnmedicalselection.net after scrutiny of applications.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Tamil Nadu DNB counselling has four listed rounds
rounds.detail: The prospectus lists Round 1, Round 2, Round 3 and Stray Round. It says this may change under DGHS/MCC/NBEMS guidelines or court orders.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 1 allotments require timely reporting
rounds.detail: Round 1 allotments are made online. Download the provisional allotment order and join the allotted DNB institution by the date and time stated in the order, with the required documents. Round 1 free exit is allowed and resignation is allowed within the Selection Committee's stipulated period.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 1 candidates can enter Round 2 after a timely non-join or resignation
rounds.detail: Candidates not allotted in Round 1, who did not register and did not choice-lock in Round 1, or who did not join or resigned a Round 1 seat within the stipulated time may participate in Round 2. The round table says there is no fee forfeiture for Round 1 non-joining/resignation within time.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 2 fills vacancies and newly sanctioned seats
rounds.detail: Round 2 fills seats left vacant because candidates did not join or were not allotted, and newly sanctioned seats arising after Round 1, by rank and communal reservation.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 2 candidates may resign or vacate only by the stated deadline
rounds.detail: A candidate retaining a Round 1 seat past the deadline, receiving an upgradation, or receiving a new allotment in Round 2 can vacate the seat by the Selection Committee's stated date. A candidate who joined in Round 2 can resign by that date. Discontinuing later triggers the stated discontinuation fee and forfeiture consequences.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 2 non-joining may forfeit the registration fee
rounds.detail: The prospectus table says an allotted or re-allotted Round 2 candidate who does not join or resigns forfeits the registration fee. It separately says that if an allotted candidate neither downloads the allotment order nor joins after Round 2 is completed, the registration fee is forfeited.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 3 is open to specified Round 1 and Round 2 candidates
rounds.detail: Round 3 fills remaining vacancies by rank list. Eligible candidates include those not allotted in Rounds 1 and 2; candidates allotted, joined or not joined in State Quota or All India Quota Rounds 1 and 2; candidates who did not register and did not choice-lock in Round 1 or 2; and State Quota candidates who joined in Round 1 or 2 but resigned in Round 2 within the stipulated date. Candidates who resigned after the Round 2 deadline are not eligible.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 3 registration costs ₹1,000 for most entrants
rounds.detail: Candidates allotted but not joined and candidates who freshly register for Round 3 must pay ₹1,000. Candidates not allotted in either Round 1 or Round 2 do not need to pay a Round 3 registration fee. The clause does not clearly settle the fee for a candidate who joined in Round 1 or 2 and seeks Round 3 upgradation; confirm this status with the Selection Committee.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB candidates with a joined seat in an earlier round can seek Round 3 upgradation
rounds.detail: A candidate with a locked-choice allotment in an earlier round who has joined can seek upgradation in Round 3.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 3 non-joining forfeits paid fees and blocks later rounds
rounds.detail: A Round 3 allottee who does not join forfeits registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee already paid, whether or not they downloaded the allotment order. A candidate allotted a seat in State Round 3 cannot participate in further counselling; the prospectus says a State Round 3 allottee who does not join cannot participate in a later round.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 3 allotment carries a join requirement and a later-year bar
rounds.detail: Clause 8(b) says candidates allotted a seat in Round 3 must join; a candidate who does not join is treated as discontinued, must pay the Clause 23(c) discontinuation fee, and is ineligible to apply for DNB Broad Specialty or Post MBBS Diploma seats in the subsequent academic year under NBE norms. Round 3 rules also state fee forfeiture and no further counselling. Clause 8(b) cross-refers to clause 23(c), which describes State Quota candidates who joined and later discontinued after the resignation period. The separate non-joining table gives forfeitures. Confirm the operative non-joining fee consequence instead of treating these differing provisions as identical. The clause refers to NBE norms “for 2022” within this 2026-2027 prospectus; confirm the operative rule for the current admission and subsequent academic year.
rounds.note: Preserved separate consequences: Clause 8(b) states the subsequent academic-year bar and discontinuation fee; Clauses 26 and the Round 3 table state immediate forfeiture and later-round restrictions.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 3 State results may wait for the MCC joined list
rounds.detail: If DGHS/MCC releases the Round 3 joined list of All India Quota candidates, the prospectus says those candidates will be blocked and State Round 3 results will then be released. The prospectus labels this subject to change.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Stray Round registration costs ₹1,000 except for candidates not allotted in any earlier round
rounds.detail: Candidates allotted but not joined or resigned in Round 1 or 2, and candidates who freshly register for Stray Round, must pay ₹1,000. Candidates not allotted in Rounds 1, 2 or 3 do not pay the registration fee. Candidates who discontinued with penalty after the stipulated time cannot enter further rounds. The eligibility list mentions allotted-but-not-joined candidates from Rounds 1 and 2 but does not expressly include resigned candidates, while the fee paragraph names “not joined / resigned”. Confirm whether a resigned candidate qualifies before registering; the wording is not reconciled here.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Stray Round eligibility depends on prior allotments and joins
rounds.detail: The prospectus lists as eligible candidates not allotted in Rounds 1, 2 or 3; candidates allotted but not joined in Round 1 or 2 of State Quota or All India Quota; and candidates who never registered and never choice-locked in Rounds 1, 2 or 3. The eligibility list mentions allotted-but-not-joined candidates from Rounds 1 and 2 but does not expressly include resigned candidates, while the fee paragraph names “not joined / resigned”. Confirm whether a resigned candidate qualifies before registering; the wording is not reconciled here.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Several DNB candidates cannot enter the State Stray Round
rounds.detail: Ineligible candidates include those holding a PG seat in State Rounds 1, 2 or 3; those holding a Round 1, 2 or 3 seat in All India Quota, a deemed university or DNB counselling by NBE; candidates allotted in an All India Quota, deemed-university or NBE DNB Stray Round; and candidates allotted a State Round 3 seat but not joined. Candidates discontinued after a deadline with penalty cannot enter later rounds.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Stray Round allotments must be joined
rounds.detail: The prospectus says this is a Stray Vacancy Round and a candidate allotted a seat according to their choices should join without fail. It says an additional round may be conducted if directed by DGHS.

rounds.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB counselling dates and round rules may change
rounds.detail: The prospectus repeatedly makes counselling procedures subject to DGHS/MCC/NBEMS guidelines and court orders. Candidates must follow the official website for current notices.

documents.name: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Tamil Nadu community certificate

documents.name: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: TNPSC/MRB selection and posting order
documents.detail: For service candidates selected through the stated competitive examination; upload the order and produce the original at admission.

documents.name: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Certified service proforma and complete service particulars
documents.detail: Government-institution medical officers must upload the service proforma certified by the designated/forwarding authority with date and seal. Complete, certify and upload it before 15th October 2026 at 5:00 PM; failure to upload means summary rejection.

documents.name: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: PwD special-category form and recent Regional Medical Board certificate
documents.detail: Upload the filled and certified special-category form and a clear copy of the recent disability certificate from a Tamil Nadu Regional Medical Board. The certificate must have been obtained within three months before application. If it is missing, the application is considered under General category only; a certificate older than three months is not considered for PwD quota. The prospectus says the form is provided in the prospectus, but no separate candidate form was identified in pages 1–60; confirm where to obtain it. documents.detail: At reporting, candidates sign a self-declaration that selection/admission is liable to forfeiture if facts were suppressed or misinterpreted. The bond declaration form records candidate/institution, course, duration, joining date, service/non-service status, service start and prior service, address, and confirms the particulars and bond are true.

documents.name: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Service-candidate bond and three sureties
documents.detail: Applicable Government Medical College bond terms in the prospectus require the stated bond amount and three sureties. For service candidates with more than five years of service after the course: two permanent Government employees of the same or higher rank and one spouse/parent; provide PAN numbers. Annexure III is the form; the prospectus says the form is exempt from stamp duty.

documents.name: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Non-service bond and three sureties
documents.detail: Required for the stated non-service Government Medical College route. The non-service bond in Annexure III requires three sureties: two permanent Government employees of the same or higher rank than the candidate and one spouse/parent. PAN numbers must be furnished. The bond is for ₹20,00,000 for a PG Diploma and ₹40,00,000 for a PG Degree; it is exempt from stamp duty under the cited Indian Stamp Act provision. The same obligation is not established here for Government Quota seats in self-financing colleges; confirm the applicable form.

documents.name: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Anti-ragging undertaking and prior-institution conduct certificate

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Relationship certificate and supporter passport

documents.detail: For NRI candidates, submit the financial supporter's NRE (Non-Resident External) bank account passbook.

documents.detail: The NRI application-document list requires the Annexure III declaration. The form identifies the guardian and candidate, states that the candidate is the guardian's ward for the 2026–2027 course, and asks the guardian to accept responsibility for the course; it requests the guardian's passport and bank-account details and relationship to the candidate. The Ward Certificate fields include age/date of birth, residence, phone/mobile/email, passport issue date/place/validity, and bank account type, name and address.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Court order declaring guardian, if applicable
documents.detail: For NRI candidates relying on a guardian, submit a copy of the Court order declaring the guardian under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: OCI card of sponsor or candidate, if applicable
documents.detail: The prospectus lists the OCI card of the sponsor / candidate; it also says the candidate seeking NRI quota must have a valid Indian passport or OCI card.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Religious and linguistic minority certificate, if applicable
documents.detail: Submit with the candidate's Nativity certificate. Annexure II says the certificate is issued by the competent Revenue Authority of the candidate's native jurisdiction and should be obtained from the rank of Tahsildar. It records religion and mother tongue. Enclosures: candidate's Nativity certificate, parent's community certificate (not applicable for forward community), and parent's study certificate.
documents.note: No profile fact tests minority eligibility; do not use category, religion or nativity as a proxy.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Candidate Nativity certificate for minority-certificate submission
documents.detail: Annexure II lists the candidate's Nativity certificate as an enclosure to the religious and linguistic minority certificate.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Same photograph as uploaded for NEET PG 2026
documents.detail: Upload the same photo used for NEET PG 2026 in the online application; the admission checklist repeats this requirement.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Postcard-size colour photograph
documents.detail: Upload a colour photograph measuring 4 × 6 inches, file size 50 KB to 300 KB.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Candidate and parent / guardian anti-ragging undertakings
documents.detail: Annexure IV reproduces MCI directions for printed undertakings, preferably in English / Hindi and a regional language. The candidate signs an undertaking that they know the anti-ragging law and have not been expelled or debarred from admission by any institution; the parent / guardian also signs an undertaking to abide by the relevant punishment if the candidate is found guilty. The annexure calls this an application-for-admission/enrolment undertaking; confirm the submission stage with the admitting institution.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: School-leaving, transfer, migration or character certificate with behaviour report
documents.detail: Annexure IV says the admission application is to be accompanied by one of these certificates, including a report on the candidate's behavioural pattern. Confirm the submission stage with the admitting institution; the annexure does not specify the Tamil Nadu online application stage.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Additional two-part anti-ragging undertaking for hostel applicants
documents.detail: Annexure IV says a student seeking hostel admission must submit the additional undertaking in Annexure I (both parts) with the hostel accommodation application.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Original certificates and scanned copies at joining
documents.detail: Candidates must produce the relevant original certificates / documents to the Head of Institution for verification at admission. Clause 23 specifically lists NEET PG admit card and score card; Aadhaar and one supporting ID; MBBS degree and Diploma certificate if applicable or provisional pass certificate; CRMI / CRRI completion; permanent or provisional Medical Council registration; Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. eligibility certificate for candidates from another university; the reminder to upload the same NEET photo in the application; and minority certificate if applicable. Bring scanned copies of the original certificates as stated in Clause 23. Clause 16(i) also requires the original NRI certificates/documents listed immediately above it at admission.

documents.name: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Self-declaration on suppression / misinterpretation
documents.detail: At reporting, selected candidates give a self-declaration that selection / admission is liable to forfeiture if suppression of facts or misinterpretation is later found.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: NEET-PG 2026 admit card
documents.detail: Upload a clear self-attested copy; produce the original at the allotted institution.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: NEET-PG 2026 score card
documents.detail: Upload a clear self-attested copy; produce the original at the allotted institution.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: MBBS degree certificate or provisional pass certificate
documents.detail: Upload a clear self-attested copy. Produce the original at the allotted institution.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Diploma certificate (if applicable)
documents.detail: Upload a clear self-attested copy and produce the original at the allotted institution. A current diploma-course completion certificate is relevant to the same-year eligibility exception.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: CRMI / CRRI completion certificate
documents.detail: Upload a clear self-attested copy; the stated completion cutoff is on or before 30th September 2026.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Permanent or provisional medical registration certificate
documents.detail: Issued by the Medical Council of India or a State Medical Council; produce the original at counselling/admission.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Tamil Nadu community certificate
documents.detail: For BC, BCM, MBC, DNC, SC and SCA candidates, certificate must be issued by the competent Tamil Nadu authority. ST candidates need a community certificate issued by the competent jurisdictional Revenue Divisional Officer.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Tamil Nadu Nativity Certificate (when claiming Tamil Nadu nativity after MBBS elsewhere)
documents.detail: Issued by the competent Revenue and Disaster Management authority of Tamil Nadu with official seal. The prospectus separately requires MBBS and the entire CRMI/CRRI period in Tamil Nadu; the relationship between these clauses is unclear.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Community certificate for either one parent (when claiming Tamil Nadu community reservation)
documents.detail: Issued by the competent Tamil Nadu Revenue and Disaster Management authority with official seal; upload alongside the candidate's own community certificate.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: TNPSC / MRB selection and posting order (qualifying service candidates)
documents.detail: The service-candidate list specifies selection through a Competitive Written Examination or Special Qualifying Examination. Upload the selection and posting order.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Completed DNB Service Proforma, certified by the forwarding authority
documents.detail: Must carry the certifying authority's date and seal and be uploaded by 15th October 2026 at 5:00 PM. For Government Medical Officers the complete service proforma must detail leave and deputation. Fill the online proforma, download it, and obtain verification and signature with official seal from the competent forwarding authority. Failure by a Government Medical Officer to upload the certified proforma results in summary rejection.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Recent Regional Medical Board certificate for PwD applicants
documents.detail: The certificate must be obtained within three months before application and uploaded with the application. A certificate older than three months, or failure to submit it, means the candidate is not considered under the PwD quota. Listed assessment boards are in the disability-centre list. Failure to upload the required PwD certificate means consideration under the General Category only, as stated in clause 4(a)(iv). The prospectus separately refers to a filled and certified special-category form, certified within three months, but the supplied annexures do not clearly identify a separate application form. Confirm whether the form and certificate are the same and obtain the correct form from the Selection Committee.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University eligibility certificate (for graduates of another university)
documents.detail: For a graduate of another university recognized by the Medical Council of India, upload the Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University eligibility certificate with the online application and produce it at counselling/admission.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Aadhaar Card and one supporting identity document
documents.detail: Upload a clearly visible Aadhaar copy plus Passport, Voter ID or Driving Licence. The prospectus says missing supporting ID results in summary rejection.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: NEET-PG photograph and postcard-size colour photograph
documents.detail: Use the same photo uploaded for the NEET-PG 2026 admit card. Also upload a 4 x 6 inch postcard-size colour photo, file size 50 KB to 300 KB.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Original certificates and scanned copies of the originals
documents.detail: Produce all originals at certificate verification/joining in the allotted institution and bring scanned copies of original certificates.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Candidate self-declaration on suppression or misinterpretation
documents.detail: At reporting, declare that selection/admission is liable for forfeiture if suppression of facts or misinterpretation is found during or after admission.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Tamil Nadu DNB service bond and three sureties (State Quota service candidates)
documents.detail: Execute the bond at admission. Two sureties must be permanent Government employees in the same or higher rank than the candidate; one must be the candidate's spouse or parent. PAN numbers are required. The prescribed form records candidate, course, service and surety particulars. The Annexure II form also describes the three sureties as Income Tax assessees. Confirm the issued bond form for your admission route. The form states that Government forbearance, time extensions, acts or omissions do not discharge surety liability and that Government need not sue the candidate before suing a surety. Each surety has Aadhaar, signature and witness fields.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Tamil Nadu DNB bond and three sureties (All India 50% Quota candidates)
documents.detail: If the Government requires service, execute the two-year bond with two permanent Government employee sureties of the same or higher rank and one spouse/parent surety; furnish surety PAN numbers. The Annexure II form also describes the three sureties as Income Tax assessees. Confirm the issued bond form for your admission route. The form states that Government forbearance, time extensions, acts or omissions do not discharge surety liability and that Government need not sue the candidate before suing a surety. Each surety has Aadhaar, signature and witness fields.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Candidate anti-ragging undertaking
documents.detail: The admission application must include the candidate's printed undertaking, preferably English/Hindi plus a regional language. The candidate acknowledges the ragging law and punishments and declares not to have been expelled or debarred. The reproduced pages describe the requirement but do not include the actual form.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Parent / guardian anti-ragging undertaking
documents.detail: A parent/guardian signs a separate printed undertaking, preferably English/Hindi plus a regional language, acknowledging the law and agreeing to abide by the punishment if the ward is found guilty of ragging. The actual form is not included in the reproduced pages.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: School-leaving / transfer / migration / character certificate with behaviour report
documents.detail: The application for admission must be accompanied by a School Leaving, transfer, migration or Character Certificate that includes a report on behavioural pattern, so the institution can keep watch where there is a negative entry.

documents.name: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Additional anti-ragging undertaking for hostel applicants
documents.detail: A student seeking hostel admission must submit an additional undertaking in the form of Annexure I, both parts, along with the hostel accommodation application. The actual form is not included in the reproduced pages.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Admissions and resignations are online only
admission.detail: Admissions and resignations must be through online mode. Offline admission or resignation is not accepted; colleges taking it may face legal consequences.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Declare that the application is accurate
admission.detail: At reporting, give the required self-declaration. The reporting declaration says selection/admission is liable for cancellation if suppression or misinterpretation is discovered during or after admission; the stated deposit/tuition forfeitures apply. Separately, hiding eligibility or non-eligibility criteria will result in cancellation of the allotment and appropriate legal/disciplinary action will be taken. Specifically, a Government/local-body Medical Officer who applies as a private candidate while suppressing service status has the application summarily rejected and any allotment cancelled.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Pay the institution fee by the allotment deadline
admission.detail: The Government Medical College annual fees and Government Quota Self-Financing institution fees are described in the Fees section. The tuition fee paid when downloading the allotment order is non-refundable if the candidate discontinues after the State Selection Committee's resignation period.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Unauthorized absence after joining
admission.detail: Unauthorized absence for 15 days or more after joining is treated as discontinuation, and the Selection Committee may fill the vacancy depending on time and NMC/MCC guidelines. If the absence extends beyond the date specified by the Selection Committee, the candidate must pay the discontinuation fee under clause 24(c).

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Check the college and seat approval
admission.detail: Allotment is only to seats affiliated to Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University or a State Private University for 2026-2027 and approved seats are to be displayed before counselling. The prospectus warns that some seats have an NMC Letter of Permission but are not yet recognized, and tells candidates to check NMC/college information before choosing. The Selection Committee disclaims responsibility for institutional approvals, infrastructure and college rules.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Discontinuation after the resignation period
admission.detail: A State Quota candidate who joined and discontinues after the Selection Committee's resignation period forfeits tuition already paid and must pay ₹10,00,000 for a PG Diploma or ₹15,00,000 for a PG Degree by Demand Draft in favour of the Secretary, Selection Committee, Kilpauk, Chennai, payable at Chennai. Until the penalty is paid in full, the institution will not relieve the candidate and will retain original certificates.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Ragging, agitation and strike are prohibited
admission.detail: Candidates joining a PG course must not engage in agitation, strike or ragging inside or outside campus. The prospectus says a candidate found participating will be expelled at any point in the course and criminal action will be taken. Annexure IV reproduces MCI anti-ragging directions.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Postgraduate course duration
admission.detail: The prospectus states PG Degree courses last three years and PG Diploma courses last two years. A candidate who completed a two-year Diploma may have a two-year PG Degree in the same specialty or a three-year degree in a different specialty. This concession does not apply after a one-year Diploma in the same or another specialty. A candidate who completed Diploma in Clinical Pathology or Diploma in Diabetology has a three-year PG Degree course.

admission.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Jurisdiction stated in the prospectus
admission.detail: The prospectus states that any legal issues, if any, are under the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Pay tuition and special fees with the allotment order
admission.detail: The selected candidate pays the full 2026–2027 tuition and special fees online when downloading the provisional allotment order. Tuition paid for the allotment order is non-refundable under the prospectus.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Check the college and course before choosing
admission.detail: Candidates are advised to check the respective college website for National Medical Commission approval, infrastructure and regulations. A Letter of Permission does not necessarily mean that a seat is recognized for the current academic year; the Selection Committee disclaims responsibility for approval and infrastructure. The Selection Committee states it will neither be responsible nor entertain any case on those approval, infrastructure or college-rule grounds.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Affiliated and approved seats
admission.detail: Allotment is limited to seats affiliated to The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University or a State Private University for 2026–2027. Seats approved by the relevant university for PG Degree / Diploma courses are to be displayed before counselling.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Join by the allotment-order deadline
admission.detail: Candidates selected in any round must download the provisional allotment order and join the course on or before the date stated in that order.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Unauthorized absence of 15 days or more
admission.detail: Unauthorized absence for 15 days or more after joining is treated as discontinuation. The vacancy may be filled by the Selection Committee depending on time and NMC guidelines. If the absence period is beyond the notified date, the candidate must pay the discontinuation fee under Clause 25(b).

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Ragging and related conduct
admission.detail: The prospectus says candidates must not take part in agitation, strikes or ragging inside or outside the college during study; candidates found participating will be expelled and criminal action will be taken. Annexure IV reproduces anti-ragging directions, including reporting incidents as a victim or witness and institutional prevention duties. The annexure describes ragging as a cognizable offence and bans it in all departments, constituent units and academic/residential/sports/canteen premises and student transportation, whether public or private, inside or outside campus.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Check the website for notices
admission.detail: All notices, notifications and publications are to be published at www.tnmedicalselection.net. The Selection Committee says it is not responsible for consequences of candidates failing to follow website information.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB seats in Government Medical Colleges and Hospitals are split 50:50 between All India and State Quotas
admission.detail: Of the recognized/permitted DNB Broad Specialty and Post MBBS Diploma seats in Government Medical Colleges and Government Hospitals, 50% are All India Quota seats allotted by the Director General of Health Services, New Delhi; the remaining 50% are allotted under the Tamil Nadu State Quota in State counselling. The prospectus separately says only eligible in-service candidates may apply for State Quota seats.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB candidates must download the allotment order and report on time
admission.detail: Download the provisional allotment order and join the DNB institution (District Headquarters Hospital or Sub-District Hospital) by the date and time stated. Failure to report physically by the deadline is treated as not joined and the seat becomes vacant.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB admissions and resignations are online only
admission.detail: All admissions and resignations must be completed online. Offline admission or resignation is not accepted. Hospitals taking offline admissions or resignations may face legal consequences at their own risk. The prospectus says resignation applies to Round 1 and Round 2 candidates.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB candidates sign a declaration at reporting
admission.detail: At reporting to the institution, submit a self-declaration that selection/admission is liable for forfeiture if suppression of facts or misinterpretation is found during or after admission.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Broad Specialty lasts three years; Post MBBS Diploma lasts two
admission.detail: The prospectus states a three-year duration for DNB Broad Specialty (Post MBBS) and a two-year duration for Post MBBS Diploma courses.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Quota service-candidate study period is treated as study leave after approval
admission.detail: The entire study period is treated as study leave after approval and permission from the Head of Department under State rules and norms.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB selected candidates pay tuition and special fees at their institution
admission.detail: Pay tuition and other special fees at admission. The prospectus does not state the amounts and says candidates will be guided through a website notification.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB stipend follows Government Orders and the institution's norms
admission.detail: All selected candidates are paid stipend under Government Orders issued from time to time for Government Medical Colleges and Hospitals, as per the concerned institution's norms. The prospectus does not give an amount.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB students are subject to anti-ragging undertakings and penalties
admission.detail: Candidates must not take part in agitation, strikes or ragging inside or outside campus. A candidate found taking part will be expelled from the course/college at any stage and criminal action will be taken. The attached MCI directions describe candidate and parent/guardian undertakings, a behaviour-report certificate, hostel undertaking, electronic affidavit/complaint records and reporting to institutional contacts.
admission.note: The MCI directions also impose prevention, awareness, counselling, vulnerable-location security, staff reporting and mentoring duties on institutions; see the full Annexure IV description. Clause 35(b) calls the extract Annexure V, but reproduced pages are headed Annexure IV.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB suppression can cancel admission and bar applications for two academic years
admission.detail: The reporting declaration in clause 19 makes selection/admission liable to forfeiture if suppression or misinterpretation is found during or after admission. Separately, clause 20 says that when suppression of facts is found later, selection/admission is liable to cancellation and the candidate cannot apply for DNB Broad Specialty or Post-MBBS Diploma seats for the subsequent two academic years. The two-year bar is not expressly stated for misinterpretation alone.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB candidates must follow the official website for updates
admission.detail: The Selection Committee will publish notices and notifications at tnmedicalselection.net and says it is not responsible for consequences of not following information posted there.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB prospectus legal issues are under the Madras High Court
admission.detail: The prospectus says legal issues, if any, are under the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB institutions must provide anti-ragging prevention and reporting support
admission.detail: The attached MCI directions require a prevention/redressal plan, meetings with wardens, students, parents, faculty and district administration including police, visible law-and-punishment notices, trained counsellors, induction and fresher/senior sensitisation, lit and secured vulnerable areas, and a named help leaflet for freshers. Institutions must keep student affidavits and complaint records, obtain staff reporting undertakings, encourage victim/witness reports, and provide mentoring and hostel oversight, including surprise room visits. At the end of the academic year, the Dean/Principal/Director must write to parents/guardians of students completing their first year about the law and penalties and ask them to discourage ragging.
admission.note: The directions name an anti-ragging committee as a help contact. No separate anti-ragging squad is identified in these reproduced pages.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Acceptance of prospectus clauses
admission.detail: Clause 38 states that an applicant is deemed to have read and agreed to all prospectus conditions and clauses and “will not have the right to challenge” any clause.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Institutional anti-ragging prevention and support duties
admission.detail: The attached MCI directions require a prevention/redressal plan, meetings with wardens, students, parents, faculty and district administration including police, visible law-and-punishment notices, trained counsellors, induction and fresher/senior sensitisation, lit and secured vulnerable areas, and a named help leaflet for freshers. Institutions must keep student affidavits and complaint records, obtain staff reporting undertakings, encourage victim/witness reports, and provide mentoring and hostel oversight, including surprise room visits. The directions state one mentor per six freshers, one higher-level mentor per six lower-level mentors, and individual daily interaction with group members; the responsible teacher coordinates surprise hostel visits with the warden.
admission.note: The directions name an anti-ragging committee as a help contact. No separate anti-ragging squad is identified in these reproduced pages.

admission.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Prospectus acceptance condition
admission.detail: The applicant is deemed to have read and agreed to the prospectus clauses; clause 36 states the applicant “will not have the right to challenge” any clause.

admission.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Legal jurisdiction
admission.detail: The prospectus places legal issues under the jurisdiction of the Madras High Court.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Resign online only
rules.detail: All admissions and resignations must be made online. Offline resignation is not accepted.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 1 free exit and resignation
rules.detail: The prospectus table allows free exit and resignation within the stipulated time, including exit without forfeiture of fees. It gives no calendar deadline; follow the counselling notice.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 exit within the stated window
rules.detail: A Round 1 seat retained beyond the stated date, a newly allotted/reallotted Round 2 seat, or a joined Round 2 seat may be vacated/resigned within the date set by the Selection Committee. Candidates who joined and resign within the Round 2 date may participate in Round 3.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 2 resignation after the deadline
rules.detail: Resigning/discontinuing after the stipulated Round 2 date makes the candidate ineligible for Round 3 and later rounds. The prospectus states a ₹10 lakh Diploma or ₹15 lakh Degree discontinuation fee after the stipulated date, and forfeiture of registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 allotment not joined
rules.detail: Whether or not the allotment order was downloaded, a candidate allotted in State Round 3 who does not join forfeits the registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee. The candidate is ineligible for later rounds.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Round 3 joined seat
rules.detail: The Round 3 table says a joined/upgraded seat cannot be vacated. A candidate who discontinues after joining forfeits registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee and pays the discontinuation fee. A State Round 3 allottee cannot participate in a later round.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Stray Vacancy Round allotment
rules.detail: A Stray seat allottee must join. Not joining forfeits registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee. After joining, the seat cannot be vacated; discontinuing forfeits those fees and requires payment of the discontinuation fee.

rules.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Discontinuation after the notified date
rules.detail: Candidates who discontinue after the Selection Committee's stipulated date forfeit registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee; State Quota candidates must also pay the clause 24(c) penalty. See the separate Round 3 and Stray rules for their additional finality conditions.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Resignation must be online
rules.detail: Offline resignations are not permitted; an offline resignation will not be accepted. The prospectus says resignation applies to allotted candidates of Round 1 and Round 2, subject to later DGHS / MCC guidelines and Court orders.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Follow the Selection Committee's stated resignation windows
rules.detail: Round-specific resignation / vacating dates are to be set by the Selection Committee. Exact dates are not in this prospectus and may change under DGHS / MCC guidelines or Court orders.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Discontinuing after the Round 2 resignation period
rules.detail: After the stipulated resignation period, a candidate who discontinues must forfeit registration fee, security deposit and tuition paid, and pay the course-specific discontinuation fee. The source says resignation after the Round 2 deadline makes a candidate ineligible for further counselling; joined candidates who are not relieved until the discontinuation fee is paid may have original certificates retained.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB resignations are accepted only online
rules.detail: All admissions and resignations are online only; offline resignations are not accepted. The prospectus says resignation applies to allotted candidates in Round 1 and Round 2.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 1 free exit and resignation are allowed within the stated window
rules.detail: The Round 1 table says free exit is allowed and resignation is allowed within the stipulated time without forfeiture. A candidate who joined may participate in Round 2 for re-allotment; eligible Round 1 non-joiners/resignees may enter later rounds.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 2 exit is time-limited
rules.detail: Candidates with a Round 1 seat who retain it past the deadline, receive an upgrade in Round 2, or are newly allotted in Round 2 can vacate by the stated date. A candidate who joined in Round 2 can resign by that date. A resignation within the deadline after joining in Round 2 is listed as eligible for Round 3.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 2 resignation after the deadline triggers penalties and bars Round 3
rules.detail: A candidate who resigns after the stipulated Round 2 deadline is not eligible for Round 3 or further counselling. The prospectus states the candidate must pay ₹15 lakh for DNB Broad Specialty or ₹10 lakh for Post MBBS Diploma, forfeit registration fee, security deposit and tuition fees, and is not allowed to vacate the seat.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 3 candidates are not allowed to vacate an allotment
rules.detail: Round 3 has no free exit or resignation. A candidate who does not join forfeits registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee already paid; after joining, the candidate is not allowed to vacate, and the stated discontinuation penalty is ₹15 lakh for DNB Broad Specialty or ₹10 lakh for Post MBBS Diploma, with registration fee, security deposit and tuition forfeited.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Stray Round candidates cannot exit or resign
rules.detail: The Stray Round has no free exit or resignation. A candidate allotted and not joined forfeits registration fee, security deposit and tuition fee. A candidate who joins is not allowed to vacate; on discontinuation the penalty applies and those fees are forfeited.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB discontinuation after the NBE / counselling deadline costs ₹15 lakh or ₹10 lakh
rules.detail: NBE candidates who discontinue on or after the date specified by NBE or counselling must pay ₹15 lakh for DNB Broad Specialty or ₹10 lakh for Post MBBS Diploma, in addition to foregoing tuition already paid. Pay the total by Demand Draft in favour of the Director of Medical & Rural Health Services, Chennai – 600 006, payable at Chennai.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB State Quota discontinuation after the resignation window costs ₹15 lakh or ₹10 lakh
rules.detail: A State Quota candidate who joined and discontinues after the Selection Committee's resignation period must pay ₹15 lakh for DNB Broad Specialty or ₹10 lakh for Post MBBS Diploma, in addition to foregoing tuition already paid. Payment is by Demand Draft to the Director of Medical & Rural Health Services, Chennai – 600 006, payable at Chennai. Until the full fee is paid, the candidate will not be relieved and the institution will retain original certificates.

rules.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: DNB Round 3 and Stray Round allotments can end later-round eligibility
rules.detail: Candidates allotted a seat in Round 3 in State counselling cannot participate in further counselling, and the prospectus says a State Round 3 allottee who does not join cannot enter a later round. Candidates holding specified State, All India, deemed-university or NBE DNB seats are also excluded from the Stray Round.

rules.title: Management/NRI MD/MS/Diploma: Earlier PG-course discontinuation trigger

annexures.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Annexure II — Disability categories and medical-course eligibility matrix
annexures.description: The table covers: (1) locomotor disability including cured leprosy, cerebral palsy, dwarfism, muscular dystrophy, acid-attack victims and other specified disabilities such as amputation/poliomyelitis. It says to consider loss of sensation in fingers/hands, amputation and eye involvement; for cerebral palsy, vision, hearing and cognitive function; and says both hands intact with intact sensations, sufficient strength and range of motion are essential. It gives less than 40% as course-eligible but not PwD quota; 40–80% as course-eligible and PwD quota; and a case-by-case statement for more than 80% if assistive devices bring it below 80% and functional/motor competency is sufficient. (2) Blindness/low vision: the table marks less than 40% as course-eligible but not PwD quota and equal/more than 40% as not eligible for medical course; its footnote says visual disability above 40% may be considered for course and quota if advanced low-vision aids such as telescopes or magnifiers bring it below 40%. (3) Deaf/hard of hearing: similar table thresholds; the footnote says hearing disability above 40% may be considered if assistive devices bring it below 40% and speech-discrimination score is above 60%. (4) Speech/language disability due to organic/neurological causes: less than 40% may pursue the course, while equal/more than 40% is marked not eligible; Speech Intelligibility Affected score must not exceed 3 (40% or below), and Aphasia Quotient must be 40% or below. (5) Specific learning disabilities, including perceptual disabilities, dyslexia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia and developmental aphasia: no quantification scale is available and the 40% cut-off is arbitrary, with more evidence needed; 40% through 80% may be eligible for course and quota based on expert-panel assessment of learning competency with remediation/assistive technology/aids/infrastructure; over 80% or severe/significant cognitive/intellectual disability is not eligible. (6) Autism spectrum: absence/mild disability or Asperger syndrome up to 60% under ISAA may be eligible where an expert panel finds the person fit for postgraduate study; quota is currently not recommended because objective assessment methods are lacking and may be considered later; over 60% or cognitive/intellectual disability/unfitness is not eligible. (7) Mental illness: absence or mild disability under 40% by IDEAS may be course-eligible; quota is currently not recommended for lack of objective assessment; the table says no mental disorder is barred from PG Medical Education if the person is eligible in NEXT/NEET-PG. (8) Multiple sclerosis, Parkinsonism, haemophilia, thalassemia and sickle-cell disease: less than 40% is course-eligible but not quota; 40–80% is course-eligible and quota-eligible; above 80% is not eligible. (9) Multiple disabilities, including deaf-blindness: consider recommendations for visual, hearing, speech/language, intellectual disability and mental illness; the printed combination formula is a + [b(90-a)/90], with a the higher and b the lower disability percentage, and may be used to compute combined disability before deciding admission/reservation.

annexures.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Annexure III — Bond agreement and candidate declaration forms
annexures.description: The blank agreement form is headed for candidates admitted to MD/MS/PG Diploma/MDS courses in a Government college for 2026-2027. It asks for execution place/date; candidate name, relationship, permanent/temporary addresses, landline/mobile/email/Aadhaar; college/course; service or non-service status; bond years and amount; and three sureties described as Income Tax assessees. The form covers certificate retention until completion of the bond or payment of the demanded sum with Government-rate interest, stipend for 24/36 months, proportionate stipend repayment if a service period is shorter, and repayment of stipend plus discontinuation fee if the course is discontinued. It includes the surety/witness signatures and PAN/Aadhaar fields. The separate declaration asks candidate name, last employer/institution, designation, PG course and duration, joining date, service/non-service status, in-service date and prior service; the candidate declares those particulars and bond are true, agrees to repay stipend with interest if incorrect, and agrees not to claim originals until bond conditions are fulfilled. The stamp-duty exemption reference differs within the prospectus: clause 37(i), p30, cites the Indian Stamp Act, 1879 (Central Act II of 1879), while the form, p39, cites the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Central Act II of 1899); no reconciliation is supplied. Sureties are not discharged by reasonable time or Government forbearance, acts or omissions; Government need not sue the candidate before suing the sureties.

annexures.title: Government-quota MD/MS/Diploma: Annexure IV — MCI anti-ragging directions
annexures.description: Annexure IV reproduces MCI anti-ragging directions. Ragging is banned in all forms in medical college/institution premises, including departments, hostels, sports/canteen areas and student transportation, inside or outside campus; institutions must observe applicable laws and take strict action against people found guilty or abetting ragging. Before admissions, advertisements must state that ragging is prohibited, the prospectus must print the rules in block letters, and candidates/parents must be sensitized to the prohibition and consequences. The admission/enrolment form must include a candidate undertaking, preferably in English/Hindi and a language used by the institution, that the candidate knows the law and punishment, has not been expelled/debarred from admission by any institution, and accepts punishment if guilty; the parent/guardian signs a parallel undertaking confirming awareness of the law and agreement to abide by punishment imposed on the ward. An electronic database of candidate and parent/guardian affidavits is described. Admission must be accompanied by a School Leaving/Transfer/Migration/Character Certificate with a report on the candidate's behavioural pattern; hostel applicants give an additional undertaking in the prescribed form. At the start of the academic session, the head of the institution convenes local officials/agencies, wardens, student representatives, parents/guardians and faculty, including police, to discuss prevention, identification and punishment. The directions call for prominent anti-ragging posters, audiovisual awareness/counselling/workshops, publicity, mapping and lighting vulnerable locations, stronger security and police patrol where needed, vacation-period campaigns, induction arrangements, and staff undertakings to report ragging. Freshers must receive a leaflet naming help contacts (including wardens, anti-ragging committee members and district/police authorities), their addresses/phone numbers, rights and reporting routes; institutions should provide professional counsellors, orientation and joint fresher/senior sensitization (including further sessions after seniors arrive in the first or second week), and encourage victims or witnesses to report incidents. At the end of each academic year, the Dean/Principal/Director sends the first-year students' parents/guardians a letter restating the law and penalties and asking them to discourage ragging. The directions describe a mentoring cell with one mentor for six freshers and a higher-level mentor for each six lower-level mentors, daily contact and support, and hostel coordination/visits. Clause 39 says the prospectus candidate will be expelled at any stage for ragging, agitation or strike and criminal action will be taken. The main text refers to an MCI direction dated 11th September 2014, while the attached notification is headed 3rd August 2009; confirm the operative reference.

annexures.title: DNB/Post-MBBS Diploma: Annexure IV: MCI directions on prevention and prohibition of ragging
annexures.description: MCI Notification No. MCI-34(1)/2009-Med./25453, dated 3rd August 2009, reproduces anti-ragging regulations. Ragging is described as a cognizable offence under applicable Central/State law and is prohibited throughout the college/university, all academic, residential, sports and canteen premises on or off campus, and in public or private transport. Institutions must take strict action against offenders and abettors. Before admission, advertisements must state the ban and punishment; the prospectus/admission booklet must print the regulations in block letters and include applicable Supreme Court and Government directions; the application and beginning-of-year booklet must explain the ban, law, punishment, prevention and redressal measures. The admission form must carry the candidate undertaking (preferably English/Hindi plus a regional language): the candidate acknowledges the law and punishment and declares not to have been expelled/debarred. A parent/guardian signs a separate undertaking acknowledging the law and agreeing to abide by punishment if the ward commits ragging. Affidavits from students and parents/guardians must be stored electronically in a database with student details and complaint records. The application must include a School Leaving, transfer, migration or Character Certificate reporting behavioural pattern; hostel applicants must also submit an additional undertaking in both Annexure I parts. Before/at the start of each year, the Head of Institution must meet wardens, student representatives, parents/guardians, faculty and district administration including police to plan prevention and identify/punish offenders. Directions include prominent legal/punishment posters across departments, hostels and vulnerable places; counselling, workshops, competitions and audiovisual awareness; media publicity; identification, lighting and security of vulnerable locations; policing at hot spots/odd hours when needed; advance induction arrangements; and undertakings from teaching, non-teaching and contract staff to report ragging. Freshers must receive a leaflet naming help contacts (including the Warden, Head and anti-ragging committee), describing rights, reporting routes and a calendar of orientation events; institutions should provide professional counselling, joint fresher/senior sensitisation, orientation, cultural/sports activities and a Mentoring Cell. The directions provide for one mentor per six freshers and a higher-level mentor for six lower-level mentors, small fresher groups with daily staff contact, and hostel group-teacher/warden coordination with surprise room visits. Freshers are encouraged to report incidents as victims or witnesses. The excerpt does not specify a separate anti-ragging squad or reproduce the undertaking forms themselves. Clause 35(b) calls the extract Annexure V, while these pages are headed Annexure IV.
